Commentary.Commentary: This ends a roller-coaster ride from today. What a match we have witnessed where it rained sixes and fours. England have won the series and when they meet next, they would like to continue their winning streak. Pakistan, on the other hand, will like to salvage their pride and put in a better performance. It takes place on the 1st of September at Leeds, at 1830 IST! Until then, take care and goodbye!

Alex Hales, Man of the Match says it is a special venue to play. (On the personal record) He says that he was not aware about it but knew that he was close enough. (On the team record) He opines that it has been a long time but the improvements in ODIs have helped them to play that way. (On his form) He confirms that it had been 5-6 tough weeks but he did practice well to achieve this feat. (On the remaining games) He ends by saying that they will like to win the series 5-0.

Eoin Morgan, England captain says it was a monumental knock by Hales to score 171 in this format. Also adds that after his struggle through this summer he really showed his talent. (On the records) He opines that all those records are good as it brings in lot of confidence. (On the team) He feels that it is a good squad which can play whenever it is needed and it will add to the success of the team. (On the remaining games) He ends by saying that they will like to play the same way and try to win the next two games.

Azhar Ali, Pakistan captain says that it was a very tough game out there as he feels that the way the English batsmen played was good. He also credits Alex Hales and Jos Buttler for their fantastic knocks. (On their fielding) He opines that the fielding was bad and the bowlers bowled no balls at the wrong moment and couldn't stop the leakage of runs. (On the remaining matches) He states that they will look to pick themselves up and improve. (On their ranking in ODIs) He feels the Test team is doing good but in ODIs they are not able to raise their game as it is a challenging format. (On the run feast) He ends by saying that it was very difficult out there but it is England who played really well today.

England can't ask for a better performance. Their batters did the job early on as Alex Hales smashed a record-breaking knock of 171 runs and he was supported nicely, first by Joe Root, then by Jos Buttler and Eoin Morgan. It was a sorry outing for the Pakistani bowlers, Wahab Riaz in particular, as the pacer finished with the second worst bowling figures in ODIs. England can take lots of positives from this whereas it will be tough for Pakistan to overcome this big defeat. There are still two matches left in this series so it will be interesting to see how the visitors fare in the remaining games.

Sarfraz Ahmed and Mohammad Nawaz got starts but just couldn't make any big impact as England kept chipping in with wickets at regular intervals. The tailenders did manage to avoid the heaviest defeat for Pakistan in the end as Amir and Yasir frustrated the English bowlers. Plunkett, Moeen Ali, Stokes and Wood all got a wicket each while Rashid grabbed two and the man in-form Woakes finished with four wickets.

Phew! With that, England have handed Pakistan a heavy drubbing. A match to forget for the visiting side though as apart from the interesting final wicket stand, nothing really looked promising for them. Earlier their bowlers were clubbed all over the park as England posted the highest ever total in ODIs and then the Pakistani batsmen eventually succumbed under the pressure. Sharjeel Khan got them off to a flying start but no one really got going from the other end. Woakes got the early breakthroughs and then, even Sharjeel fell to Woakes after his quick fifty.
